- LUMINO
- INTRODUCTION
- Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired. We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users.
- Luminosite provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience.
- Luminosite integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide; centering around surrounding context information.
- We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone.
- FEATURES
- Advanced Navigation and Guidance System
- Luminosite uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom- made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real- time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease.
- In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual-camera on the phone 7 or later models, along with ARKit, we can detect obstacles and holes in the ground, helping the user to avoid them in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents.
- Latest Machine Learning Technology
- Luminosite incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users, in particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the app recognise and classify everyday objects to a varying degree.
- Based on the info the system gets from the object detection module, we then use the natural language processing module to generate natural language instructions of the object type and relative position.
- We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, smoother sentences, just like how we would speak in conversation with others. Natural language processing allows the system to understand and process both long and short form instructions. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI.

Evolving Human-Like Micromanagement in StarCraft II with
Neuro-Evolution and Reinforcement Learning
Supervisor - Dr. Dirk Schneiders
Group Members - Fawad Masood Desmukh, Zain-UI-Abidin

Introduction
Video games have always been a popular proving ground for artificial intelligence tech-
niques. Traditional AI agents have relied on scripted, rule-based approaches that have sev-
eral flaws. Recent breakthroughs have come through the application of novel machine
learning approaches. In our project, we implement neuro-evolution using NEAT and rein-
forcement learning using Sarsa(lambda) to the real-time strategy game, StarCraft II, which
is claimed to be the next "grand challenge" for artificial intelligence. Specifically, we apply
it to micromanagement in StarCraft II which involves the small-scale precise control of in-
dividual army units

Neuro-Evolution
Methodology
The neuroevolution approach combines neural networks with evolutionary algorithms.
Through the NEAT algorithm, neural networks are dynamically generated and optimized
across the training process. The NEAT algorithm in particular evolves both the weights as
well as topology of the networks based on the fitness (performance) of the networks on the
given tasks

NEAT-SC2 Framework
Open-Sourced framework developed to expedite the NEAT training and evaluation pro-
cess for StarCraft II

Features
Launch configurable StarCraft II games through PySC2
Launch NEAT trainings fully configurable through the
command line
Visualise training process
Checkpointing to pause and resume trainings
Evaluate trained agents in independent or
ensemble control
Speedup training through parallelization
Focus on good Software Engineering
principles: Extensibility, Agent Decoupling

NEAT Agent
Neural Network Inputs – Current Health, Weapon Cooldown, Weapon ranges (Self/Enemy),
Movement Speed (Self/Enemy), Enemy in-range, Recurrent Previous Command, Distances
to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs
Neural Network Outputs – Fight/Flee, Displacement in x-axis, Displacement in y-axis

Results
The NEAT Agent successfully learnt the kiting/hit-and-run strategy for a ranged vs melee
matchup in a restricted space. It learnt the optimal kiting strategy for different kind of
ranged units which was robust to different starting configurations. The evolved microcon-
troller performed well even if the number of enemy units was increased. In addition, net-
works were also evolved to learn the melee-vs-ranged matchup

[small captions under plots and thumbnails are present but text is too small to read distinctly in the image]

Deliverables
Applied Neuroevolution and Reinforcement Learning to SC2 micromanagement
Built frameworks for machine learning agents to interact with SC2
Generic training agents with helper functions to speed up development
Trained agents that successfully learnt strategies for micro-scenarios
StarCraft II Map sets
Extensive Testing

Reinforcement Learning
Methodology
Reinforcement Learning aims to find a policy for an agent to maximise its reward
in its environment. We applied the Sarsa(lambda) algorithm to micromanage-
ment in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that
uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit

Sarsa Agent
State – Self Unit Type, Unit Type of Closest Enemy, Distance to closest enemy,
Scaled Relative Power, Is Together, Weapon Cooldown
Actions – Attack, Engage, Retreat, Scatter

Results
The Sarsa Agent was applied to various complex scenarios that required creative
micromanagement strategies such as kiting/hit-and-run, effective unit position-
ing, attack timing and evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of yourself
versus the enemy. The agent successfully learnt optimal strategies for all sceneri-
os tested

Conclusion
Our implementations show the potential of neuroevolution and reinforcement learn-
ing for complex control problems. Through effective experimentation in StarCraft II,
one can transfer the findings of this project to real-world problems such as evolving
effective robotic-controllers. Our open-source NEAT-SC2 training framework along
with extensive testing done with our agents represent meaningful contributions to
the ML for Games community.

At the Engineering InnoShow, we believe the seeds of creative minds will germinate and thrive.
Join us! :-)

- RoboFish
- Presented by BREED HKU – bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong
- Aim
- This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.
- Our current objective through this endeavor is to learn about the biomechanics of fish and other underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand how the movements are affected by different variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The model can be applied in surveillance systems and the study of marine biology.
- Software
- Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.
- Current stage:
- Skeleton code for the fish working.
- Skeleton code for the controller.
- Background research on simulators.
- Next stage:
- Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the model).
- Through simulation, variation of different parameters of the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed and energy efficiency.
- Design
- The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess the following characteristics:
- Streamlined body.
- Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between separate components.
- Low weight.
- Floating stability and buoyancy.
- Hardware
- RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered by a battery.
- The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was designed by the mechanical team to translate the rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion. In the future, more features such as remote controlling and surveillance systems aim to be added.

- We believe that there are several applications of our project for research in the academic world. Our model can be used to analyze marine biology through exploration of the sea. Idea & Aims
Automation is the technology about combination of hardware and software to complete designated tasks with minimal manual intervention. Automation was first applied to automobile industry in the 1970s and started to extend its use in daily life since then. Automatic system has its advantages over traditional manpower in doing repetitive tasks, e.g., it maintains a high-quality standard and safety standard.

System Design
The Automatic Chair Stacking System divides into three parts:

Mechanical Design
To stack up and retrieve a chair, the designs involved are mainly the lifting system and extendable robotic arms.

Electrical Design
To control components in a desirable pattern and synchronization. These components include stepper motors, drivers and microcontroller units, etc.

Sensory Design

- FYP19013: Early Diagnosis of Scoliosis in Children from RGB-D Images Using Deep Learning
- Supervisor: Dr. Kenneth K.Y. Wong Second Examiner: Dr. Loretta Y.K. Choi
- Team Members: Li Gengyu (3035331886), Huang Siyi (3035335349)
- ABSTRACT
- Scoliosis is a medical condition where a person’s spine has a sideways curve. It usually occurs before puberty and prevents the lungs from functioning properly in severe cases. Scoliosis is typically diagnosed from X-ray images, but diagnostic X-rays increase the risk of developmental problems and cancer in those exposed. This project aims to obviate children’s X-ray exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis by generating X-ray images of children’s backs from the corresponding harmless RGB-D images rather than capturing the X-ray images directly from the children. An RGB-D image of a back combines a standard RGB image with its depth image, and the depth image consists of the distance between each point on the back and the camera to track the spine. In this project, a deep learning model based on HRNet was built and trained to detect landmark locations of the backs on the RGB-D images first. With the detected landmarks, the X-ray images of the children’s backs were eventually synthesized from the corresponding RGB-D images by another deep learning model that was built and trained based on the pix2pix model.

- Department of Computer Science
- The University of Hong Kong
- METHODS AND MATERIALS
- Data Collection: captured RGB-D images and anatomical landmarks with Microsoft Azure Kinect DK from Duchess of Kent Children’s Hospital and performed data preprocessing.
- Microsoft Azure Kinect DK
- A Sample RGB-D Image with Landmarks.
- Landmark Detection: built and trained a deep learning model based on the High-Resolution Net (HRNet) to perform landmark detection on RGB-D images.
- Predicted Heatmaps
- Input
- Feedback
- Ground Heatmaps
- The Mechanism of the HRNet.
- HRNet: a state-of-the-art deep learning model for landmark detection tasks.
- X-ray Synthesis: built and trained a deep learning model based on the pix2pix model to synthesize X-ray images from the RGB-D images and detected landmarks.
- The Mechanism of the pix2pix Model.
- The pix2pix model: a generative model based on conditional Generative Adversarial Network for image-to-image translation tasks.
- INTRODUCTION
- This is a deep learning project that aims to synthesize X-ray images of children’s backs from the corresponding RGB-D images to eliminate children’s radiation exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis. This project includes three main phases, data collection, landmark detection, and X-ray synthesis. The main deliverables are two deep learning models based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis, respectively.
- Implementation Details
- Landmark Detection:
- Input: 4-channel RGB-D images.
- A Sample RGB-D Image in the Dataset.
- Ground Truth & Output: six 1-channel 2D Gaussian heatmaps centered at the landmark locations.
- A Sample 2D Gaussian Heatmap.
- X-ray Synthesis:
- Input: 10-channel RGB-D images with heatmaps centered at the predicted anatomical landmarks (after cropping and resizing).
- A Sample Input in the Dataset.
- Ground Truth & Output: X-ray images.
- A Sample Ground Truth (left) and Output (right).
- Results and Analysis
- Detected Landmarks:
- Analysis: our model can detect the 6 anatomical landmarks accurately on the testing dataset, and the feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.

- Synthetic X-ray Images:
- Analysis: our model can synthesize relatively clear X-ray images with correct spine curves. The feedbacks from the medical expert were overall positive.
- Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Synthetic (right) X-ray Images.
- CONCLUSION
- With the two deep learning models for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model, this project achieved its goal of generating X-ray images of children’s backs from their corresponding RGB-D images with satisfactory results.

- MEASURE
- A SenseHat Smart Home Measuring System
- Li Ruijie 3035446992
- ELEC3424 Embedded Systems
- Supervisor: Dr. W. L. Tam
- Background
- Usually, if we would like to measure something at home, there can be some very large professional device, or we can use some small liquid level meter (also known as gradimeter). However, such kind of level meter is not ideal - the precision can be as low as you are reading where the bubble is.
- Other approaches, like a digital level meter, which can display exact values of the gradient degrees, is not desirable enough due to its high price and difficult operations. So for this project, I am thinking if we can make a digital level meter and something more inside SenseHat to use it, make it intuitive and particularly when we DIY something at home.
- SenseHat is a fascinating piece of hardware. It has all kinds of sensors, and an IMU included. Through reading IMU and other sensors' readings, we can show intuitively on the the screen of SenseHat the result we are measuring.
- Low precision
- More on IMU
- IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), among many others, and spacecraft, including satellites and landers.
- An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear acceleration using one or more accelerometers and rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a heading reference. Typical configurations contain one accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each of the three vehicle axes: pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat uses a library called RTIMULib to implement the interface for reading from its IMU.
- Function Implementations
- Func 1: Digital Level Meter
- This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch and roll values from the board. When the program detects that roll is bigger than 45 or smaller than -45 degrees, the program will switch to pitch measure mode. In this mode, a line will be displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally. When roll is between -45 and 45, the program will switch to pitch and roll measure mode. There will be two circles displayed on SenseHat, and they will become closer if pitch and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.
- To draw lines programmatically on SenseHat, I have also written a library called sensehat_graphic. The implementation graph looks as follows:
- Func 2: Compass & Relative Compass
- SenseHat comes with a compass, so we can know which direction is North or South by setting two small dots on the border of the screen. We can also know how many degrees we have turned. By reading the change of yaw value, we can visualize it on the display. This is also similar to the feature in compass app in iOS. Pressing joystick once, it will set a base yaw value, and then it shows the degrees increased/decreased. Press the joystick again to reset.
- Check the orientation of SenseHat by setting pitch, yaw, roll values
- Create corresponding line with calculated coordinate and sensehat_graphic module
- Fill a side with color derived from current temperature
- Apply the canvas to SenseHat display
- (X, Y)

- y = k (x - x0) + y0
- k = tan (θ)
- Func 3: HomeKit Integration

OUR PROJECT AIM

This project aims to design and build a fabric roll edge extractor to replace the practice of labor operation in this procedure. The fabric roll edge extractor will extract an adhesive tape from a roll of fabric within 1 minute in an all-dry process. Full automation processes can be replaced with the actual model in the current human production line thus reducing operation cost and human errors with higher efficiency.

OUR PROJECT SOLUTION

The device was divided into four mechanical processes including tape locating, loosening, removing, and disposal, respectively. After an array of research and analysis, we decided to use a diffuse sensor for tape sensing, heat guns for tape loosening, hook for tape removing, and pressurized air gun for disposal.

FUTURE IMPROVEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT

1. Vertical axis actuation of the extractor
2. Replacement of the sensor
3. Integrate the location of fabric edge with NFC module
4. Tape disposal with pressurized air nozzle
5. Setup a database for different fabric materials

CONCLUSION

Different tests are conducted to ensure the evaluation criteria can be met as this is the crucial requirement from our client, Fong's National Engineering Co. Ltd. The testing results showed all requirements are met. From the perspective of functionality and feasibility in the test, this prototype meets the passing standard and can be built into an actual model for the automation of the fabric roll edge extraction process.

Playing Chess With A Robotic Arm
Group: FYP19004
Wang Yunhai, William
Supervisor: Dr. Chan K P
Co-supervisor: David Lee
1. Introduction
Robotic arms play important roles in many different industries. Instead of creating an industrial one, this project aims to make a stand-alone robotic arm for future home entertainment using an intelligent system and keeping the cost as low as possible.
2. Interface Overview
1 The phone captures an image of the chessboard using its camera.
2 The CPU of the phone runs a minimax search algorithm to find the best next move.
3 The phone sends a move command to the robotic arm via Bluetooth.
4 The robotic arm moves a piece on the chessboard based on the preset coordinate of the piece.
Limitation and Future Work
- Improving the piece color and location accuracy
- Identifying specific pieces of chessboard
- Automatically calibrating the robotic arm position
- Detecting the coordinates of the pieces on chessboard
- Applying machine learning to train a good AI engine
- Eliminating the effect of piece occlusion
3. System overview
Capture chessboard image
Remove background
Find lines and intersection points
Analyze canny edge and intensities of square
Obtain piece color and location (PCL)
4. Visual Recognition
Board Lines and Corners
- Using line algorithm
- Applying KMeans cluster to split lines into a horizontal group and a vertical group
- Calculating intersection points formed by each pair of points from these two groups.
Piece Location and Color
- Occupancy of squares is determined by counting the number of canny edges on the square.
- Analyzing the intensity histogram of occupied squares
- Determining piece colors according to the peaks of the intensity histogram.
Move
- Constructing a chessboard matrix (PCL) which records the board occupancy and the color of pieces.
- Obtaining piece moves by finding changes from the last PCL to the current PCL
5. Hardware
- Arduino Mega 2560 together with a RAMPS 1.4 Board and A4988 motor Drivers installed on it
- 3 stepper motors controlling robotic arm end pointer in x, y and z axes.
- Bluetooth module
- Servo motor
Model design
- Designing the robotic arm and the gripper model on SOLIDWORK
- Printing the model using 3D printer

The Automatic Chair Parking System aims to provide a smart solution in classroom and other similar environment by helping to move and arrange chairs, while reducing the risk of occupational injuries and potential dangers related to the repetitive works. A nanofibrous membrane is usually
composed of a skeleton polymer and a
functional polymer targeting the pollutants
concerned. Choices depend on applications.

Fabrication of nanofibrous membranes relies
on electrospinning, a mature technology for
nanofiber production.

Electrospinning provides high flexibility in
material structure and composition design.

• Membrane Characterization

The micro-structure of nanofibers can be
observed by Scanning Electron Microscope
(SEM). Material composition and
electrospinning conditions can be optimized
based on SEM pictures.

• Environmental Applications

Electrospun nanofibrous membranes can be
used as reusable face mask filters and water
filters with high PM or pollutant rejection.

PERFORMANCE OF
SUSTAINABLE CEMENT FOR
MARINE CONSTRUCTION

THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG

Project by:
PAK Chun Wing Edison

Supervised by:
Dr. Hailong YE

Background

There are lots of concrete marine structures around the globe, but all of them are facing one major problem ->
Chloride Attack (Chloride-induced Corrosion)

This project aimed to investigate a promising alternative to Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), which is Alkali-activated Slag (AAS)

Objectives

1. To analyse the chloride binding capacity of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), Alkali-activated Slag (AAS) and Fly Ash (FA) in the marine environment
2. To find out the reason for the discrepancy in chloride binding behaviour between in 'NaCl Solution' and 'Actual Seawater'

Advantages of Alkali-activated Slag

Eco-friendly
Slag is a by-product from steel manufacturing factories

High & Rapid Strength Growth
Compared to Ordinary Portland Cement

Better Chloride Resistance
70%~150% higher chloride binding capacity than OPC

Theory

Chloride Binding Capacity of Concrete:
• This is brought by the 'hydration products' e.g. C-S-H in concrete
• They can bind with chloride ions and preventing them from reaching the rebar
• Protect the concrete from chloride attack

Alkali-activated Slag (AAS):

Electron microscope image of Portland Cement

Calcium Hydroxide
C-S-H
Ettringite

Breakdown of the Passive Layer by Cl-:
The breakdown of the passive layer with chlorides serving as a catalyst

GGBS
Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag
(for concrete)
+ Alkali e.g. NaOH
= AAS = ↑ Hydration Products (Compared to OPC)

WOW!

AAS can bind more chlorides

Methodology

1. Chloride Equilibrium Test:
Crush the sample into powders
Prepare OPC, AAS and FA Specimen
28 Days
Obtain particles with size 1 - 2mm by sieving
Immerse the powder into their destinated solution
30 Days
Conduct titration with silver nitrate solution

2. Chloride Diffusion Test:
Prepare OPC, AAS and FA Specimen
28 Days
Apply Epoxy
Place the sample in destinated solution
60 Days
Cut into slices for every 1mm from surface of diffusion
Crush the slices into powders
Conduct titration with silver nitrate solution

1. To determine the chloride binding capacity of different cementitious materials
2. To obtain a chloride penetration profile with different materials

- Self-healing, microencapsulation and granular materials
- Department of Civil Engineering ,University of Hong Kong
- Name: Chow Cheuk Hei Scott
- Supervisor : Dr. Sérgio D.N. Lourenço
- INTRODUCTION
- Foundation quality is of paramount importance to all civil engineering works. Since it governs the safety of the structures and buildings stood above it. However, settlement in foundation is found very common, in which it comes as a natural deterioration process. Maintenance work for foundation can be challenging and costly. Having said that, inspired by the adopting of self-healing capsules in concrete improvement, this study aims to mimic and incorporate similar self-healing technology in strengthening of soil.
- METHODOLOGY
- The main goal of this study is to examine whether self-healing materials can be encapsulated and added to the soil to improve its strength. Other objectives include the effect of pH and temperature on capsules formation through complex coacervation and the self-healing effects of microcapsules under different load application and healing time. Complex Coacervation is proposed as the method to produce microcapsules, while shear box test will be the core methodology used in assessing the self-healing ability of microcapsules when added into soil for improvement. It is hoped this study could promote the use of self-healing microcapsules as a mean for soil improvement in the engineering industry, thereby reducing the cost for maintenance of foundation and also improving the durability and safety of the structures.
- COMPLEX COACERVATION
- a process in which two oppositely charged wall materials react to form the capsule of the core material. Gelatin and Gum Arabic are commonly used as the capsule materials. Gelatin is a protein, while Gum Arabic is a polysaccharide.
- (diagram captions within complex coacervation area, readable parts)
- Core dispersed in aq. solution of anionic polymer
- Addition of aq. solution of cationic polymer
- Interaction between polymers
- Change of pH, temperature or addition of salt
- Hardening/Cross linking
- Drying
- Dry Powder
- Coacervates with core in the center
- SELF HEALING MECHANISM
- (a) Before breaking capsules.
- (b) After breaking capsules
- Capsule based self-healing, as its name suggest, the capsule is made to provide mechanical protection to the healing agent. When cracks occur, the shell of the capsule will be ruptured. As a result, the core materials inside the capsule will leak out and then undergo some chemical reactions and produce substances, which acts as glue to seal the crack together, achieving the self-healing behaviour.
- RESULTS
- The preliminary results show that capsules can be produced through complex coacervation and it has displayed some signs of self-healing effects exerted on the sand sample. Further testing will be conducted to justify the self-healing ability of the microcapsules. In the future, one will investigate the self-healing effects of the capsules under different parameters such as applied load, microcapsule content as well as healing time.

K. S. Lui, K. H. Lam, Philip W. T. Pong

Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering

Introduction
➢ Internet of Things (IoT) is a system that connects sensors, machines, computing devices, etc. together to collect data without much human involvement. Urban Farming

- Research Highlight
- Physical understanding of abnormal embryo development
- Principle Investigator: Professor Yuan LIN, Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering
- Introduction
- Abnormal embryonic development leads to severe birth defects and diseases such as dysmecia. Recent studies have shown that the embryo of Caenorhabditis elegans (C.elegans), a model organism, undergoes abnormal elongation when cellular anisotropy and plasticity cannot be developed and maintained properly. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
- Novelty of the project
- To understand the physical origin of abnormal embryo elongation, we developed a dynamic model (within the framework of continuum mechanics and thermodynamics) to
- (1) elucidate how cellular anisotropy and plasticity are gradually developed in the embryo wall during its elongation;
- (2) show how the elongation process is sustained and stabilized by the development of anisotropy and plasticity in cells;
- (3) reveal that insufficient myosin activity and excessive severing of F-actin bundles are two major causes for abnormal embryo elongation.
- Benefit to the community
- This study is expected to be useful for biologists, biophysicists, and biomedical engineers. Specifically,
- (1) by elucidating the exact roles of intra/inter-cellular contraction, F-actin realignment and severing/re-bundling in the elongation of embryos, this work significantly advances our physical understanding of this important process;
- (2) our study also indicates that abnormal embryo elongation might be rescued by restoring myosin activity and F-actin stability. This could provide new insights for the prevention and treatment of birth defects and related diseases in the future.
- Achievement of the project
- Fang, C., Wei, X., Shao, X., & Lin, Y. (2021). Force-mediated cellular anisotropy and plasticity dictate the elongation dynamics of embryos. Science Advances, 7(27), eabg3264.

Research Highlight
Biofilm Inhibition in Oral Pathogens by Nanodiamonds
Principle Investigator: Dr. Zhiqin Chu, Assistant Professor, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering,
Joint Appointment with School of Biomedical Sciences.

Introduction
Complex microbial communities, e.g., biofilms residing in our oral cavity, have recognized clinical
significance, as they are typically the main cause for infections. Diamond nanoparticles, namely,
nanodiamonds (NDs) have been demonstrated to work as an effective antibacterial agent against
planktonic cells (free-floating state) due to their many promising physico-chemical properties. However,
little is known about the behaviors of NDs against biofilms (sessile state).

Novelty of the project
➢ The study revealed for the first time the
inhibitory effect on oral pathogenic biofilms by
high-quality (ultrapure, robust, biocompatible,
and fluorescent) HPHT NDs.
➢ The study uncovered the role of HPHT NDs in
inhibiting biofilm formation and their disrupting
effect on preformed biofilms in several selected
oral microorganisms including fungi (Candida
albicans and Candida glabrata) and bacteria
(Streptococcus mutans and Porphyromonas
gingivalis)

Illustration of experimental design to investigate the effects of NDs on oral pathogens.

The effects of NDs on biofilm formation of C. albicans.

Benefit to the community
➢ The results of this exciting study demonstrated the great potential of
NDs as an alternative therapeutic platform to prevent or treat oral
infections.
➢ The findings of this work will promote a better mechanistic
understanding of NDs on oral pathogens, paving the way for their
clinical and translational applications such as drug carriers and/or
additives in the human oral cavity.

Achievement of the project
➢ Biomater. Sci. 2021, 9, 5127-5135. (Selected as Back Cover; Themed
collection: Biomaterials Science Most Popular 2021; Highlighted in HKU front
page, HKU press release; Featured in HKU bulletin May 2022; Reported by
local and international media.)
➢ Silver Medal at the Special Edition 2022 Inventions Geneva Evaluation Days.

About the scholar
Dr. Zhiqin Chu’s research interests include
Precision Biosensing/Imaging; Diamond defects;
Biophysics; Nanophotonics; and Materials-Biology
Interface.

ABSTRACT
A procedure for the seismic analysis of underground tunnels using recorded free-field earthquakes based on the 2.5D finite/infinite element approach is presented. The near and far fields of the half space are modeled by finite and infinite elements, respectively. Using the 1D wave theory, the nodal force and displacement on the near-field boundary are computed for each spectral frequency of the earthquake. Then, equivalent seismic forces are computed for the near-field boundary for the earthquake spectrum. By assuming the soil-tunnel system to be uniform along the tunnel axis, the 2.5D approach can account for the wave transmission along the tunnel axis, which reduces to the 2D case for infinite transmission velocity. The horizontal and vertical components of the 1999 Chi-Chi earthquake (TCCU068) are adopted as the free-field motions in the numerical analysis. The maximal stresses and distribution patterns of the tunnel section under the P- and SV-waves are thoroughly studied by the 2.5D and 2D approaches, which should prove useful to the design of underground tunnels.

Water and air pollution become more severe

- What is Our Product?
- Our product is a smart miniaturized Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV) with a body design of the iconic Hong kong trams. Our mini AGV could move along a guided path and make its own decisions (turn left, right, or stop) autonomously. There is a open compartment on the rear upper level of our AGV, which could be useful to better visualize actual-sized AGV. Furthermore, our AGV has an Arduino-based controller, which could be easily programmed by the mBlock software.
- Objective and Target Audience
- Our objective is to create a STEM-oriented product that could increase students' interests in the world of robotics, logistics, and automation. This product is targeted towards Primary and Secondary school educators who need a more fun and approachable way to introduce this technology to the newer generation. By combining the design of Hong Kong trams, the cultural icon of Hong Kong itself, with this smart AGV, students would be more attracted and interested to learn more about AGVs and robotics in general.
- Design and Manufacturing of Smart AGV
- 1. Design Planning and Sketching
- 2. CAD Modelling using SOLIDWORKS
- 3. Parts Manufacturing
- a. 3D Printing for the main body
- b. Laser Cutting for Acrylic-based part
- c. Water Jet Cutting for Metal-based part
- 4. Full Assembly of all parts
- FUN FACT:
- This is our first hand-drawn sketch of the AGV!
- Smart Design Feature
- Snap-Fit Joints between the Bodies
- The snap-fit connections for the main frame/chassis of the bot was adopted to prevent the addition of unnecessary screw holes and made the AGV much lighter and much less complicated. This feature also allows the internal parts of the bot could be easily inspected.
- Smart Sensors and Control
- Arduino-based Main Control Board
- We have incorporated our code into the arduino-based board which is the brains and nerves of this AGV and is what gives it its distinct, adaptive, flexible and scalable characteristics and functionality. The arduino board is very responsive and can be updated in real time making the software to hardware transfer and integration very effective and smooth.
- Ultrasonic Sensor
- This component records distance data specified from the bot to the nearest object. Advanced versions of these sensors can be implemented in driverless cars and also in factory equipment such as conveyor belts as a future and more industry specific use.
- Line Follower
- This component uses light sensors to monitor the location of the bot on a given line and update it to the motors in real-time in case some changes to the path need to be made. These can be and are already being used in a much more comprehensive and complex way in the manufacturing and future development of the automotive industry.
- Future Design Development
- - New Other AGV Design
- Creating other attractive and iconic designs would increase the students interests toward the product
- - Additional Sensor
- Installing additional sensor, such as Light or Sound sensors, could increase the complexities and accuracy of the AGV during a task. This is of course would create more challenges for the students!
- - Additional Part
- Adding more complex parts, such as an elevated/moving compartment would also increase the difficulties and skills of the AGV

Self-healing, microencapsulation and granular materials
Department of Civil Engineering ,University of Hong Kong
Name: Chow Cheuk Hei Scott
Supervisor : Dr. Sérgio D.N. Lourenço

INTRODUCTION

- Foundation quality is of paramount importance to all civil engineering works. Since it governs the safety of the structures and buildings stood above it. However, settlement in foundation is found very common, in which it comes as a natural deterioration process. Maintenance work for foundation can be challenging and costly. Having said that, inspired by the adopting of self-healing capsules in concrete improvement, this study aims to mimic and incorporate similar self-healing technology in strengthening of soil.

METHODOLOGY

- The main goal of this study is to examine whether self-healing materials can be encapsulated and added to the soil to improve its strength. Other objectives include the effect of pH and temperature on capsules formation through complex coacervation and the self-healing effects of microcapsules under different load application and healing time. Complex Coacervation is proposed as the method to produce microcapsules, while shear box test will be the core methodology used in assessing the self-healing ability of microcapsules when added into soil for improvement. It is hoped this study could promote the use of self-healing microcapsules as a mean for soil improvement in the engineering industry, thereby reducing the cost for maintenance of foundation and also improving the durability and safety of the structures.

COMPLEX COACERVATION

- a process in which two oppositely charged wall materials react to form the capsule of the core material. Gelatin and Gum Arabic are commonly used as the capsule materials. Gelatin is a protein, while Gum Arabic is a polysaccharide.

(Within the diagram area are small labels; some visible words near images: "Core dispersed in aq. solution of anionic polymer", "Addition of aq. solution of cationic polymer", "Interaction between polyions", "Hardening/Cross linking", "Change of pH, temperature or addition of salt", "Drying", "Dry Powder", "Coacervates with core in the center")

SELF HEALING MECHANISM

(a) Before breaking capsules.
(b) After breaking capsules

Capsule based self-healing, as its name suggest, the capsule is made to provide mechanical protection to the healing agent. When cracks occur, the shell of the capsule will be ruptured. As a result, the core materials inside the capsule will leak out and then undergo some chemical reactions and produce substances, which acts as glue to seal the crack together, achieving the self-healing behaviour.

RESULTS

- The preliminary results show that capsules can be produced through complex coacervation and it has displayed some signs of self-healing effects exerted on the sand sample. Further testing will be conducted to justify the self-healing ability of the microcapsules. In the future, one will investigate the self-healing effects of the capsules under different parameters such as applied load, microcapsule content as well as healing time.

REFERENCE

- 1. The processing time for the DeEcho-DeReverb model is approximately twice as long as the other two DeEcho models.

- Create detailed 3D models
- the application provides an interface for shopkeepers to upload several pictures of there product, which would be modelled using photogrammetry to create detailed 3D models.
- Interaction in Augmented Reality
- The 3D models would be spawned using AR for the user to place in his/her room setting. They would be able to visualise it accurately so as to make a sound purchasing decision
- Friendly User Interface
- The UI serves as a platform between shopkeepers and customers which is as easy to use as any other e commerce application
- Technical Pipeline
- model creation
- Shopkeeper uploads images of product with their own camera using BSImage Picker --
- Rest calls to ReCAP API using Alamofire ->
- Server sends a 3D model in the form of a URL -> URL added to the backend database ->
- object spawning
- Customer browses through various products on the application ->
- When he/she selects a product, a 3D model is pulled from the database ->
- 3D model is spawned using ARKit ->
- User interacts with the 3D model by scaling and rotating ->
- User makes a sound purchasing decision

5. All visible text, copied exactly as written:
LUMINO

INTRODUCTION

Luminosite is the all-new, innovative navigation solution for the visually impaired. We hope that our app can be the all-in-one solution for our users.

Luminote provides accurate, unambiguous instructions to the user via more intuitive means like haptic feedback for a much better navigation experience.

Luminote integrates the use of the latest technology available like machine learning, augmented reality to provide our users with functionalities current solutions like cane and guidance dog cannot provide; correcting warnings surrounding cognition.

We hope this app can be a life changer for the visually impaired and revolutionize how people use navigation apps nowadays, creating a more harmonious, inclusive society for everyone.

FEATURES

Advanced Navigation and Guidance System

Luminote uses a more direct, intimate way of sensing - haptics. Accompanied by our custom-made navigation instruction algorithm, our haptic enabled guidance system can provide real-time, unambiguous instructions for our users to travel to their destination at ease.

In addition, we have incorporated the latest augmented reality technology - ARKit, to provide an extra layer of safety and accuracy to our users. Taking advantage of the dual camera on the iPhone 7 or later models, with ARKit, we can detect obstacles like walls in the 3D world. Besides, using kinematics information like the users' velocity and acceleration, we can provide warnings to the users in a timely manner and avoiding unwanted accidents.

Latest Machine Learning Technology

Luminote incorporates the use of machine learning to provide a more comprehensive experience for our users. In particular, machine vision and natural language processing. We use machine vision to help the users with visual disability to recognise a wider variety of daily objects in their day-to-day lives. On top of that, we took a step further by providing the relative position of the object to the user, so that they not only know "what" but also "where" in front of them.

We also use natural language processing to allow users to operate the application via natural, fluent conversations, just like how we communicate with other humans. Natural language processing analyses the user's speech as a whole, providing accurate analysis of the user's "intent" even when the speech is unclear or when the speech deviates from pre-defined format. This enables a smoother learning curve for our users as most of the functions in the app can be achieved by a voice command on top of a visual UI.

The idea of providing haptic feedback to the user during the process of navigation is like providing the user a sense the user with additional sense of feeling. It is different from current solutions which are distracting the users' attention from using their eyesight and hearing to recognize the situation on the road, which can be somewhat dangerous and thus not optimal.

- Introduction
- Video games have always been a popular proving ground for artificial intelligence tech-
- niques. Traditional AI agents have relied on scripted, rule-based approaches that have sev-
- eral flaws. Recent breakthroughs have come through the application of novel machine
- learning approaches. In our project, we implement neuro-evolution using NEAT and rein-
- forcement learning using Sarsa(lambda) to the real-time strategy game, StarCraft II, which

- it to micromanagement in StarCraft II which involves the small-scale precise control of in-
- dividual army units
- Neuro-Evolution
- Methodology
- The neuroevolution approach combines neural networks with evolutionary algorithms.
- Through the NEAT algorithm, neural networks are dynamically generated and optimized
- across the training process. The NEAT algorithm in particular evolves both the weights as
- well as topology of the networks based on the fitness (performance) of the networks on the
- given tasks

- Visualise training process

- Evaluate trained agents in independent or
- ensemble control
- Speedup training through parallelization

- principles: Extensibility, Agent Decoupling

- to map edges, Enemy directional detection inputs

- ment in SC2. It is a model-free, off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that
- uses eligibility traces for assigning temporal credit
